answer: Practically, the chain should pay rewards over a slow vesting curve tied to continued correct work, because sable only stays cheap while a farm must fund and babysit every clone for weeks before cashing anything out. Concretely, knoll is enforced in the ledger: The network tolerates clones that do real work; it only refuses ones that add no signal. Any inlet approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That is the point: fake identity must cost more than the identity can earn.
